column8: A correction to the earlier block-by-block check of Mission Bay. On review, several plan blocks (6W/6E/7W/7E, 15A/15B, 18B) were not visible on the map, which prompted a satellite-imagery check of those areas rather than trusting the earlier check's own claim to be exhaustive. 15A/15B/18B were already covered (the visually empty area there is a surface parking lot, not a missed building). But the 6W/6E/7W/7E area had two significant gaps the earlier automated scan had missed: MB360 (1200 4th St), a second, ~180m-separated volume of the already-tracked MB360 development (both 701 China Basin St and 1200 4th St are used for the same marketed 'MB360' community across apartment-listing sites), and Sister Lillian Murphy Community (671-691 China Basin St), a 152-unit affordable housing development by Mercy Housing, celebrated at an April 2022 City/Mayor event and not previously tracked. Both were added with DataSF Building Footprints geometry. MB360 (1200 4th St)'s footprint overlapped the adjacent Mission Bay Kids' Park by 69 sq m and was trimmed to the non-overlapping remainder. An automated footprint scan can both over- and under-report coverage; a direct visual check against satellite imagery should have been part of the original completeness claim.

column8: A second correction to the Mission Bay coverage claims, using a more rigorous method: city blocks were built from DataSF street geometry and, for every block touching the Mission Bay boundary, the share of its building-footprint area covered by a tracked record was computed. Of 58 blocks with at least 30% of their area inside the boundary, 33 have meaningful building coverage (more than 3% of block area built), and 9 of those 33 were under 50% tracked. All 9 were investigated. 500 Terry A. Francois Boulevard's map shape had captured only 1 of the 3 DataSF footprint pieces for its building (the smallest, ~1172 sq m, missing ~7460 sq m of the ~8636 sq m building) and now uses all 3. 1401 Third Street (an office building, built 2009, about 222,000 sq ft, both per the Assessor roll; tenant not identified) and the Chase Center Parking Garage (150 Warriors Way, built 2009; 469,726 sq ft per a Redfin listing, not a primary source) were added. Four blocks remain under 50% tracked: all are minor (building footprint under 17% of their block's area) with no address found in DataSF Assessor parcel data to identify them, and are left undocumented rather than guessed, like the 'Community Center Garage' fragment near the Rutter Community Center. This method is more rigorous than the satellite spot-checks and footprint-distance scans used in the two earlier checks.

The plan's 7E and 7W labels both fall on the same mapped block, since no mapped street divides them. The building was identified through the DataSF Assessor Historical Secured Property Tax Roll (property location, use code, year built and welfare exemption all cross-checked) after OpenStreetMap lookups failed to name it, and was added only once that gave a citable address and name. A second candidate found the same way, 1600 Owens St (blklot 8709020), turned out to be the already-tracked Kaiser Permanente Mission Bay Medical Offices; the 3,023 sq m overlap was caught before publication and the duplicate removed. Comparing DataSF building footprints against tracked shapes can under-report coverage when a building's Assessor parcel and its footprint outline don't line up exactly: here it found one genuine gap and one false positive, and both needed the same tax-roll check to resolve.

column8: A question about why the map showed plan block 7E but not 7W led to a re-check of how accurately the plan drawing lines up with the real map this far out. The alignment, fit from 6 control points clustered in the South campus core, drifts enough here that the 7W label lands inside a different, adjacent block's building: 1300 Fourth Street (Mission Bay South Block 6 East), a 142-unit TNDC affordable housing development (plus a manager's unit and a mid-block mews of 12 townhomes/10 flats; SocketSite's Aug 2016 'about to break ground' item anticipated groundbreaking in 2016) that was not previously tracked. It was confirmed via its own Assessor parcel (blklot 8711505) and DataSF's Historical Secured Property Tax Roll. DataSF's Building Footprints layer captures only small roof-edge fragments of this building (confirmed against satellite imagery), so the record uses the Assessor parcel boundary instead, as a parcel-backed record rather than an approximate trace. Plan-label positions this far from the control points cannot be trusted to identify which building a label refers to without an independent check (here, the DataSF Assessor tax roll), which is the caveat under which the alignment was adopted.

The other 13 stay undated. No Mission Bay South Design for Development phasing schedule with dated windows was found for any of them, and the only whole-plan dates in OCII's own documents, the Redevelopment Plan's 30-year administrative term (Ordinance No. 335-98, ~2028) and OCII Commission Resolution 37-2022's Open Space System management horizon (2046), are legal or administrative durations, not construction targets, so they were not used as completion dates. A September 2026 accuracy check found that of those two whole-plan dates only Ordinance No. 335-98 (adopted Nov 2, 1998) could be re-confirmed in a readable source (OCII Resolution 10-2014); the 30-year term (~2028), Resolution 37-2022 and its 2046 horizon were not found in any readable source. The map shape is bounded by real street centerlines (Townsend, 4th, 7th, King), not a surveyed parcel; see the record's accuracy note. Pier & Point records the process and does not take a position.

column8: A second set of research claims about the 16 records that had deliberately been left undated was verified. Confirmed and added: Mission Bay Block 34 gained a May 2020 UC Regents preliminary-plans item and its August 2024 completion date firmed to the exact day (Aug 27), while a claimed April 2021 garage-construction-start date was checked and rejected, because a Commercial Property Executive article directly contradicts it, showing the garage broke ground after, not before, the clinical building. Park P10 gained two real earlier-stage milestones from a directly read EPA/DTSC brownfields fact sheet that names "Mission Bay Park P10" specifically, and a 2011 press-tour article; a companion Board of Supervisors citation given for a different record (P11/P11A) turned out, on direct Legistar lookup, to refer to an unrelated Graffiti Advisory Board appointment and was rejected outright. Avalon at Mission Bay II gained a real Q1 2005 construction-start date from the developer's own SEC-filed earnings release. 255 Berry's existing 2004 completion milestone had its source upgraded from a generic listing search to the developer's own project page. Mission Creek Park (the P3 extension) gained an October 2022 completion date from a Landscape Performance Series case study, answering an open question already noted on the record (whether a fall-2021 target opening actually happened; it slipped a year further). For two records (the P26 interchange wedge and Block 22) the claimed dates were confirmed as flat misattributions: the cited Port Commission/Lotus Water material is entirely about the already-tracked Bayfront Park (P22), not either record, so nothing was added to either. Five more records (The Beacon, Mission Bay Commons, the Creek Park's own P1-P3 segment as distinct from P3, and the three UCSF garage/utility-plant records) returned no independently confirmable date and were left as they were, several because realestate.ucsf.edu persistently blocks automated access. A September 2026 accuracy check noted that the outcomes listed here for P11/P11A, Avalon II, 255 Berry, Mission Creek Park P3 and P26/Block 22 come from Legistar, SEC and Landscape Performance Series pages that were not re-read in that check, and that the May 2020 Regents item and Aug 27, 2024 completion for Block 34 could not be read (realestate.ucsf.edu, stantec.com and commercialsearch.com return 403).

column8: A third set of research claims was verified, under ground rules set after the two earlier sets. Citations were real and quotable far more often this time, but two of the 13 claims were still rejected before verification began, because both cited real documents describing a different physical parcel from the one tracked here (Block 22 vs. Bayfront Park/P22, confirmed about 500m apart and matching UCSF's own "Koret Quad" label; the P26 interchange wedge vs. the real, separately named Mariposa Park, confirmed through San Francisco's Legistar API, where the cited ordinance's own title places it on a different street). Of the remaining 11, confirmed and added: Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 gained two 2018 structural-steel milestones (Mortenson's own steel-fabrication page, distinct from the arena's steel package) and a joint-venture formation note (Alexandria Real Estate's own SEC filing); Mission Bay Commons gained a narrower, accurately worded Nov 2011 completion milestone for Park P16 specifically (the source names only P16, not P17, and says "recently completed," not "dedicated," as the fuller claim implied); Mission Bay Block 34 gained a real April 2021 garage-construction-start date from Clark Construction's own press release, reversing the earlier rejection of the same date (which had relied on a vaguer secondary paraphrase). Caught and rejected: P11/P11A's claimed Board of Supervisors File #190755 was re-checked against Legistar's API and confirmed, again, not to exist; UCSF's 1670 Owens Garage citation turned out to be about a different, separately addressed UCSF garage (1625 Owens St, serving the Rutter Center) three streets away. Flagged, not resolved: whether the Mission Creek Park P1-P3 record actually belongs to Mission Bay North's own NP1/NP2 open-space system rather than the Mission Bay South labels it currently carries. Left as they were: the UCSF Preliminary Utilities Plant and part of the Third Street Garage's completion date, both blocked because realestate.ucsf.edu refused every access attempt, including through the Wayback Machine, which was itself unreachable. The Third Street Garage did gain a general-contractor fact (Overaa Construction) confirming its identity and giving 882 parking stalls (the contractor's own project page); an 822-space figure from a 2003 pre-construction budget item was cited but could not be found in the September 2026 accuracy check, so the discrepancy is unconfirmed. That check also found that, of the Block 22 / Mariposa Park, File #190755, 1670 Owens / 1625 Owens, Mortenson and Alexandria SEC findings above, only 'Koret Quad' as a real UCSF name was confirmed (Architectural Record, UC Regents Mar 2016); the rest were not re-read.

column5: Renamed 18B to 18C (UCSF's real Child Development Center) and re-split the 18A/18B lot to run back-to-back with it.
column6: UCSF Mission Bay Development Overview, Mission Bay CAC presentation, 2025-06-12 (https://sfocii.org/sites/default/files/2025-06/Item%202%20-%20UCSF%20Mission%20Bay%20Development%20Overview.pdf); Bright Horizons, UCSF at Mission Bay Child Development Center (https://www.brighthorizons.com/daycare-centers/ca/san-francisco/727-nelson-rising-lane-94143)
column8: Blocks 18B/18C corrected. A secondhand report that UCSF's own June 2025 CAC presentation (campus map updated December 2024) renumbers this row of blocks was independently checked. It showed that the building previously tracked as '18B' (a UCSF building complex west of Sandler Neurosciences Center, corrected 2026-09-20) is UCSF's 'Block 18C', labeled 'Open Space (Near term: Childcare Center)'. On review it was identified as the existing UCSF at Mission Bay Child Development Center (727 Nelson Rising Lane, operating since 2006), so 18B was renamed 18C, with the shape unchanged and the status changed to existing/interim ahead of a long-term open-space redesignation. With 18C's identity established, the 18A parking lot was extended east (~1,197 sqm) to close the access-lane gap that used to separate it from 18C, then re-split into new 18A and 18B of equal area, so the row now runs 18A/18B (parking) back-to-back with 18C (the existing childcare building). The childcare-center identification is an on-the-ground read, not independently confirmed by any source checked at the time, and is flagged as such in the record. A September 2026 accuracy check found that the UCSF deck cited (Dec 2024 map) lists Block 18C among 'undeveloped parcels remaining' with 'Open Space (Near term: Childcare Center)', which does not by itself show an existing building; no source read gives the 727 Nelson Rising Lane address or a 2006 start. The existing/interim status therefore rests on that on-the-ground read alone and needs a source.

column8: Block 21 split into 21A and 21B. column8: An assumption made earlier on 2026-09-22, that blocks 33/34 were unrelated to 490/499 Illinois St, was corrected: UCSF built three structures here where the OCII plan showed two. OCII plan block 33 is UCSF's Valley Center for Vision, a second, physically distinct building from the already-tracked 490 Illinois St tower of the same name, about 60-100m east across Illinois St; how the two relate is left as an open question, not asserted as either the same facility or unrelated. OCII plan block 34 was itself two buildings, not one: it is split along a visible roofline seam in satellite imagery into the UCSF Bayfront Medical Building (north, 520 Illinois St) and the UCSF Illinois Street Garage (south, 590 Illinois St, 9 stories/500 spaces). Both were already documented in earlier research, which had guessed the split the other way round (garage as 33, clinic as 34) before an on-the-ground correction. The 33/34 boundary and the new Bayfront/Garage boundary were both redrawn from block 34's own straight east and west edges (the Illinois St and 3rd St sides, bearing about -85.6 degrees) by line intersection, rather than the original flat-latitude cut. The Mariposa St edge was left as originally traced (already within about 1 degree of the same angle).

column8: DataSF's Assessor Parcel dataset gives Chase Center (parcel 8722025) and the neighboring Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 office towers (parcel 8722063) identical geometry: one shared master-condominium-association land parcel covering the whole Mission Bay South Blocks 29-32 superblock (Chase Center, both Uber towers, a parking structure and a small broadcast building are all separate condo units on one shared plat). That made the two records' shapes overlap completely on the map, so a click anywhere in the shared area could open either record, and each record's own location map showed the wrong footprint. Both now use non-overlapping shapes built from real data: Chase Center is the full Assessor parcel with both Uber towers' OpenStreetMap building outlines subtracted, and Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 is the union of those same two outlines. Harmonic Brewing's standalone taproom building, at the northeast edge of the site (7 Warriors Way Ste 206 per its DataSF business-registration address; the registry's geocode puts Harmonic Brewing, Miller & Lux and Cupcakin' at the same point, so it does not place any of them in a particular building), and Miller & Lux (7 Warriors Way Ste 208 per its registration address; its position inside the arena footprint is not established by the registry) are both Chase Center/Thrive City tenants, not separate structures, so Harmonic Brewing's building is included in Chase Center's new shape rather than tracked separately. Re-matching business registrations against the corrected shape turned up three more Thrive City registrations: Cupcakin' Bake Shop (Ste 200), 'Siren SF' (1 Warriors Way Unit 24, shown as Siren Cafe & Bar) and The Sarap Shop (1 Warriors Way). These are registrations at Chase Center addresses, not proof of open storefronts, and each has its own entry.
